title: The vocoder was built to shrink and secret speech
body: Bell Labs' vocoder (Dudley, 1939) analysed speech into slow-changing bands so it could cross cheap channels, and fed into SIGSALY, the encrypted system that carried Roosevelt and Churchill's calls with one-time-pad noise from vinyl records. Analysing voice into parameters served compression, secrecy and, later, robot voices in music. One invention, three careers.
